rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable type — developers integrating LLMs into production apps — who demonstrably pay for reliability tooling (Galileo, TruLens, LangSmith all have paid tiers), and the explicit HN 'I would pay' signal is unusually direct. Buildability is the constraint: a genuinely useful confidence/uncertainty layer requires either multi-sampling, cross-model consistency checks, or a calibrated classifier — none are trivially assembled in a week with just Claude + Stripe, and naive approaches risk being worse than useless in the regulated domains (legal, medical) where the pain is sharpest. The build_gate for buildability_with_ai (scored 5, floor is 6) is the deciding factor keeping this at validate — the technical approach must be validated before committing to build.
solution_plan: WHAT: A per-call API wrapper that takes an LLM response and returns a confidence flag (high/medium/low/uncertain) by running lightweight consistency checks — e.g. asking Claude to self-assess, cross-checking key claims against a second sampling, and returning a structured verdict. BUILD: The factory sets up a Claude-powered prompt pipeline (consistency probe + structured output), wraps it behind a simple API endpoint (using a serverless host like Val.town or a minimal Railway deployment), and publishes a Stripe-linked pricing page with a free-tier trial — no operator coding required. SELL: Reach developers via HN Show HN post, targeted posts in AI developer Discord communities (e.g. Buildspace, LangChain Discord), and direct outreach to GitHub repos actively using LLM APIs — outreach batches go out only after the operator approves them. MAINTAIN: API calls, billing, and usage tracking run through Stripe + serverless + Claude; support questions handled by a Claude-powered email responder; the only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing monthly billing anomalies. CAVEAT: This is genuinely hard to do well — a superficial confidence score that misfires will get rejected fast by developers; validate by shipping a free prototype to 10 developers and measuring whether they find it useful before building paid infrastructure.
notes: build_gate unmet: buildability_with_ai scored 5 (floor 6). The core technical challenge — producing a calibrated, trustworthy confidence signal — is non-trivial with standard Claude + prompt tooling alone. Validate the approach with a working prototype before committing to build.
